summary: Leopold von Schroeder (1851–1920) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Tartu, Tübingen, and Jena under Leo Meyer, Ernst Kuhn, Berthold Delbrück, and Rudolf von Roth, later holding professorships at Tartu, Innsbruck, and Vienna.

Leopoldo de Eguílaz y Yánguas (1829–1906) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He earned a Dr.iuris at Complutense University of Madrid (~1860–1864) and was appointed Professor of General and Spanish Literature at the University of Granada in 1864.
Lepel Henry Griffin (1838–1908) worked in Indology and history and archaeology. Educated at Windlesham House School and Harrow School, he served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1860 to 1889.
Leslie C. Orr is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She served at Concordia University, where she was attested in 1994 and as Professor from 2019 to 2021.

Leslie S. Kawamura (1935–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar and Tibetologist. He completed his PhD at the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Guenther (~1970–1975) and served as a professor at the University of Calgary from ~1976 to 2011.

Levi H. Elwell (1854–1916) was an Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Amherst College and Yale University, later serving as an Instructor in Latin at Amherst College from 1877 to 1878.

Levi McLaughlin is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned degrees at Toronto and Princeton. He studied under Susumu Shimazono and Shigeru Nishiyama, and was appointed Professor at North Carolina State University in 2012.

Lewin Bentham Bowring (1824–1910) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at East India Company College and Fort William College, served in the Bengal Civil Service (1843–1870), and was Chief Commissioner of the Government of Mysore (~1862–1870).

Lewis Doney is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University and SOAS under Ulrich Pagel. He held posts at the British Museum, NTNU, Ruhr University Bochum, and the University of Bonn, becoming Professor of Tibetology in 2021.

Lewis Hodous (1872–1949) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Case Western Reserve, Hartford Seminary, and Halle-Wittenberg, later serving as head of Fukien Union Theological Seminary and as Chinese Department professor at Hartford Seminary (1917–1945).

Lewis Lancaster is a Buddhist studies scholar and Sinologist who studied at Roanoke College, Claremont School of Theology, and Wisconsin–Madison under Richard Robinson and Edward Conze. He taught at UC Berkeley (~1967–1998) and University of the West.
Lewis Robert Stacy (1787–1848) was an Indology and history/archaeology figure. He entered the East India Company in 1804 and served as a Lieutenant-Colonel in the Bengal Army from circa 1804 to 1848.

Lewis Sydney Stewart O'Malley (1874–1941) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a B.A. from Hertford College, Oxford (~1893–1897), and served as a Magistrate and Collector in the Indian Civil Service from 1898 to 1924.

id: P:Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk
summary: Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Lhagpa Phuntshogs is a Tibetologist who served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991), secretary-general of the Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000), and Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center (2000).

Lhakpa Tsering is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He has served as a Professor at Tibet University and as an Assistant Professor of Tibetan Language and Literature at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Li-Juan Su is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a master's degree at National Taiwan Normal University and pursued doctoral studies at National Chengchi University, where she was a PhD student in 2024.

Li-ching Chang (1936–2010) was a scholar in Sinology and linguistics. She taught Mandarin Chinese at the University of Washington, Tunghai University, Bryn Mawr College, Harvard University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Swarthmore College.
Liang Cai is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Daniel Boucher and was attested as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas in 2014.

Libbie Mills is an Indologist who completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 2011. She is attested as a teacher of Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto in 2020.
